item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Sharif left Pakistan on a **somewhat stronger macro trajectory than the crisis baseline he inherited**, but the improvement was mostly **stabilization at the top-line macro level**. Inflation fell, reserves rebuilt, and growth recovered, yet poverty, debt, weak governance, and the power sector kept the recovery fragile and incomplete.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Pakistan entered 2024 from a crisis trough, not a healthy starting point** | World Bank | 2023-10-03 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/10/02/fiscal-reforms-are-critical-for-economic-stability-sustainable-growth-in-pakistan | The inherited baseline was bad: FY23 had contracted, with floods, import controls, political uncertainty, high prices, and weak confidence. This matters because any 2024 improvement has to be judged against a severe starting point. IDs: 5B.10

- **IMF says the SBA restored stability, with reserves up and inflation down** | IMF | 2024-04-29 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/04/29/pr24130-pakistan-imf-executive-board-completes-second-and-final-review-sba | Pakistan had a primary surplus ahead of target, inflation was declining, and reserves had risen from about $4.5B to about $8B. This is strong evidence that the economy was on a better trajectory than at the start of 2024. IDs: 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.3

- **World Bank says FY24 stabilized and growth recovered, but poverty rose** | World Bank | 2024-10-10 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank | The economy stabilized, growth recovered to 2.5%, and lower inflation/prudent policy helped, but poverty still increased to 40.5%. This supports a “better than inherited, but still not broadly strong” judgment. IDs: 5B.10, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **IMF says 2024 reform efforts improved macro credibility and resilience** | IMF | 2024-09-27 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr | The IMF said growth returned, inflation fell to single digits, reserve buffers were rebuilt, and policy rate cuts followed disinflation. This is the clearest 2024 evidence that the trajectory was materially stronger than the inherited one. IDs: 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.7

- **Renegotiating power deals was a concrete response to an external cost shock** | Reuters | 2024-09-07 | https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/pakistan-renegotiating-power-deals-to-cut-costs-minister-says-3606192 | The government moved to cut “unsustainable” electricity tariffs because households and businesses were buckling under energy costs. That is direct evidence of adapting policy to external commodity and utility pressures rather than ignoring them. IDs: 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.3, 5B.7

- **World Bank says the recovery was still too weak to restore living standards** | World Bank | 2024-04-02 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/01/pakistan-implementing-an-ambitious-credible-and-clearly-communicated-economic-reform-plan-critical-for-robust-recovery-p | Growth was expected to be only 1.8%, poverty was around 40%, and the outlook was constrained by SOE losses, import management, weak confidence, and global energy/food-price risks. This is strong counterevidence that the economy had been put on a clearly strong trajectory by that point. IDs: 5B.10, 5B.9, 5B.8

- **IMF says the structural problems were still severe by late 2024** | IMF | 2024-10-10 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152 | The IMF still described a narrow tax base, weak governance, very low investment, insufficient health and education spending, and climate vulnerability. This is the main reason the answer is only “somewhat stronger,” not “clearly strong.” IDs: 5B.10, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.6, 5B.7

- **World Bank financed shock resilience for poor households and climate-sensitive sectors** | World Bank | 2024-06-20 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/20/pakistan-world-bank-approves-535-million-for-crisis-resilient-social-protection-and-climate-smart-growth-in-the-livestoc | The Bank approved financing to strengthen crisis-resilient social protection and climate-smart growth, explicitly linking Pakistan’s policy response to flood and climate shocks. This supports a more resilient trajectory, though it is institutional support rather than proof of Sharif’s personal execution. IDs: 5B.10, 5B.8, 5B.9

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a 2024 source that proves a durable, household-level improvement in employment or living standards by year-end.
- The evidence is strongest at the **macro-stabilization** level; it is weaker on whether the gains had already become broad-based or self-sustaining without IMF support.
